source.title: From Directions to Cones: Exploring Multidimensional Representations of Propositional Facts in LLMs
source.authors: Stanley Yu; Vaidehi Bulusu; Oscar Yasunaga; Clayton S. Lau; Cole Blondin; Sean O'Brien; Kevin Zhu; Vasu Sharma

page_placements.theme: Distributed, redundant and compensatory contributions to behavior

record.tranche_reason: Applies multidimensional concept-cone interventions to propositional truth representations in LLMs, an extension to a new concept and setting. It tests whether truth-related behavior can be mediated by multiple directions, but not toy-model superposition itself.
record.gate_note: The paper measures truth-related interventions using one- to five-dimensional cones and reports cosine similarities between cone axes and a DIM direction. These results bear on V6's single- versus multidirectional representation question. It does not test sparse overcomplete feature storage, polysemantic neurons, capacity competition, or SAE features. Layerwise ASR is described in text but shown only as an aggregated figure without model-specific numerical values; it is not included as rows. Sentiment and toxicity experiments do not bear on the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains gradient-optimised 'concept cones', sets of orthonormal directions that each flip Yes/No truth answers, and reports answer switching rate (ASR) and cosine similarity to the difference-in-means (DIM) direction. It does not test whether superposed features are 1-D or multi-dimensional (V6). Each cone axis is itself a 1-D direction, so the result says that several 1-D directions can mediate one behaviour. That is not an irreducibly multi-dimensional feature, and the authors say it does not prove the representation is nonlinear. The vectors are optimised to induce the behaviour (steering), not found arising naturally. No polysemanticity, sparse overcomplete storage, toy model or SAE is studied. Toy Models of Superposition appears only in the reference list.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that multi-dimensional concept cones (up to 5-D in larger models) causally mediate truth judgements beyond a single DIM direction, with low KL divergence on Alpaca prompts. They add that this does not necessarily prove truth is represented nonlinearly, that the axes lack semantic labels, and that smaller models show lower ASR.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses gradient-based concept-cone discovery and truth-response interventions, rather than the toy-network feature-sparsity and interference experiments in the original source.
record.method_sensitivity: ASR changes with model size and cone dimension; the paper also reports stronger one-dimensional interventions at later-middle layers and at the final token position.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimised cones of up to 5 orthonormal directions each flip truth answers. ASR is near 100% in Qwen 7B/14B and Gemma 9B, but falls to 27–67% in Qwen 3B and Gemma 2B at higher dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single behavioural concept (propositional truth) can be causally mediated by multiple orthogonal residual-stream directions, not only one DIM direction.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code will be open-sourced on Github but gives no URL
record.problems: Experiments cover two model families and a narrow operationalization of truth limited to simple, unambiguous propositions. The paper itself notes weaker ASR for smaller models and says it has not found semantically meaningful labels for the cone axes. Table 1 reports no uncertainty values; variability is shown in boxplots for Monte Carlo samples. The paper's stated model-scale limitation conflicts with the listed 14B models and its limitation text says 1.5B–7B parameters.
record.rows_left_out: The layerwise one-dimensional ASR result in Figure 2 is described as concentrated around 60–75 percent normalized depth and strongest at the final token position, but is aggregated across models and given without numerical values. PCA visualizations in Figures 4–5 are exploratory and do not report a separate quantified test of V6.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, sparsity transition or geometry.
All of it: no neurons, capacity or importance analysis.
All of it: no polysemanticity analysis.
All of it: no SAEs or neuron-distribution analysis.
All of it: no SAE features.
Whether superposed features are 1-D directions or multi-dimensional objects. The cones are sets of 1-D steering directions, not multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Preprint. The limitations section says the models were 1.5B–7B, which conflicts with the 14B model used. Mean KL values (Table 2) are not rows but bear on no version. The sentiment and toxicity cone attempts failed, and these are irrelevant to superposition.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features in excess of dimensions, feature interference, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular superposition geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity, limited-capacity competition, and the relation between feature importance and dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Whether real models spread features across neurons or contain sparse features recoverable by a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.

The study tests whether multiple one-dimensional directions can independently mediate truth-related behavior, but not whether superposed features themselves are one-dimensional or multidimensional, nor whether such features are superposed.

rows.subject: Qwen 14B
rows.operation_detail: Measured Answer Switching Rate after interventions using cones of the stated dimension; directions were sampled from each cone.
rows.baseline: Baseline prompts answered truthfully; the paper says these were almost always the total prompts because accuracy was nearly full.
rows.note: One-dimensional comparator; this result alone does not establish multidirectional mediation.
rows.check: ASR of optimised steering/ablation vectors per cone dimension (Table 1). This is a steering effect on truth answers, not a measure of whether superposed features are 1-D. The values match Table 1. ASR as defined counts only ablation flips.

relation.reason: Superposition sources appear in the references and related background; the experiments neither test nor use superposition as an established mechanism.

tranche.reason: The study measures optimized truth-response interventions, not feature overlap, capacity competition, SAE recovery or irreducibly multidimensional superposed features. Its results do not test V1–V6.

source_check.notes: Table 8's Qwen-2.5-9B caption does not identify a model listed in Table 6; no replacement checkpoint can be established from the text. Multiple effective steering directions do not establish irreducibly multidimensional superposed features, and the authors explicitly caution that their results do not prove nonlinear truth representations.

statements.problem: The cone-intervention finding is supported, but the stated 27–67% range excludes Qwen 3B's 78.9% ASR at dimension 4.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 14B, Qwen 7B, and Gemma 9B with cone dimensions 2–5
reader_labels.reason: High ASR with multidimensional cones supports multiple directions mediating truth-related behavior (R02–R05, R07–R10, R17–R20); the near-zero DIM similarities for additional axes are consistent with additional directions (C02, C04–C05, C07–C09, C11–C14). This supports multidirectional mediation, not a claim about the dimensionality of individual superposed features.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Qwen 3B and Gemma 2B at cone dimensions 2–5
reader_labels.reason: ASR is lower for these smaller models and declines at some higher dimensions, so multidirectional mediation is weaker and model-dependent (R12–R15, R23–R25).
